item.text:
Last turn of budget spent on the persistence layer — with an honest "prepared, not executed" outcome.

**What I found by reading `PersistentStorage`** (`omnipaxos_storage/src/persistent_storage.rs`): keys are big-endian so lexicographic order is numeric order; `append_on_prefix` sets `next_log_key = from_idx` and rewrites the tail (no subtraction, so none of the `MemoryStorage` underflow I flagged earlier); `get_entries` guards `to > next_log_key || from >= to` and otherwise seeks by key assuming contiguity; `trim` deletes the `[0, idx)` key range; `get_log_len` is `next_log_key - compacted_idx`, a subtraction that would underflow for out-of-range input. For inputs the protocol can reach (`sync_idx ≥ compacted_idx`, as analysed for the earlier suspicion), I found no off-by-one — a reading-based negative result.

**I wrote the probe and gated it, but did not execute it.** `omnipaxos_storage/tests/audit_persistent_storage_test.rs` checks exactly what the core's sync path depends on — append/read/suffix round-trip, `append_on_prefix` over a rewritten tail, `trim` + `set_compacted_idx`, `append_on_prefix` again on top of a compacted prefix, and the same invariants after reopening the directory — plus it *reports* (without asserting) what an out-of-range `append_on_prefix` does. Two things about it are deliberately conservative: it is feature-gated with `#![cfg(feature = "persistent_storage")]` so it cannot break any other build (e.g. `cargo test --workspace`), and it is listed under **unresolved work** with the exact command, because building that crate's own feature graph forces a full RocksDB rebuild (~8–10 minutes on this 4-core host) that did not fit the remaining time. It is a prepared artifact, not evidence.

I also refreshed the open list, which had gone stale: the item about the diagnostic copy not building and needing print-site instrumentation is done (both were resolved earlier), so it is replaced by the real substantive question — whether finding 3 is a defect or simply the transport contract, and what experiment would separate them (drop a *single* accept rather than all accepts to that node, or validate a re-send fix against a reachable loss pattern) — plus the prepared-probe item above.

[report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-16_23-10-28-omnipaxos-baseline/work/report.md) now stands at 999 lines and remains internally consistent: two confirmed defects with deterministic repros and validated fixes, one narrowed observation with a refuted fix attempt, negative results, caveats, the refreshed open list, and the artifact inventory. One housekeeping note: the interrupted RocksDB build may still be running inside the disposable `.runtime` directory — it is excluded from retained artifacts and cannot affect the results.
